description:
Error paths for commands that had none: exit status and diagnostic for bad usage.

Network failures are not here: Wasmtime cannot make HTTP requests locally, so they are covered by
the Golem integration tests.

cases.name: join: unsorted input and missing file
cases.script:
printf 'b 1
a 2
' >/tmp/l; printf 'a x
' >/tmp/r; join /tmp/l /tmp/r; echo status=$?; join /tmp/nosuch /tmp/r; echo status=$?

cases.name: ln: missing target and existing link
cases.script: ln /tmp/nosuch /tmp/l; echo status=$?; : >/tmp/t; ln -s /tmp/t /tmp/s; ln -s /tmp/t /tmp/s; echo status=$?

stderr.text:
ln: failed to access '/tmp/nosuch': No such file or directory
ln: failed to create symbolic link to '/tmp/t': links to absolute paths are unsupported in bash-tool; use a relative target
ln: failed to create symbolic link to '/tmp/t': links to absolute paths are unsupported in bash-tool; use a relative target

expected.reason: fixture (symlinks): links to absolute paths are refused, since WASI cannot create them

cases.name: mkdir: existing and missing parent
cases.script: mkdir /tmp/d; mkdir /tmp/d; echo status=$?; mkdir /tmp/a/b/c; echo status=$?; mkdir -p /tmp/a/b/c; echo status=$?

cases.name: printf: missing and extra arguments
cases.script: printf '%s %s\n' only; printf '%d\n' x; echo status=$?; printf; echo status=$?

stderr.text: sh: /tmp/nosuch.sh: running a script file is unsupported in bash-tool; use `source /tmp/nosuch.sh` or `sh -c`

expected.reason: fixture (script-files): running a script file by path is refused; source it or use sh -c

cases.name: sleep: invalid intervals
cases.script: sleep x; echo status=$?; sleep -1; echo status=$?; sleep; echo status=$?

cases.name: yes: write error to a closed pipe

stderr.text: curl: (3) URL rejected: Malformed input to a URL function

expected.reason: curl reads [ in a URL as a glob range and points at it; bash-tool reports the malformed URL, with the same status

cases.name: curl: invalid time values
cases.script: for v in -1 -0 +3 ' 3' .5 5. nan inf abc ''; do curl -s -m "$v" http://127.0.0.1:1/; echo "m=[$v] status=$?"; done; curl -s --max-time -1 http://127.0.0.1:1/; echo status=$?; curl -s --connect-timeout nan http://127.0.0.1:1/; echo status=$?; curl -s --retry-delay -1 http://127.0.0.1:1/; echo status=$?

cases.name: wget: invalid time periods
cases.script: for v in -1 -1m 1e3 nan inf 1e300 abc 3x ''; do wget -q -T "$v" http://127.0.0.1:1/; echo "T=[$v] status=$?"; done; wget -q --timeout=-2 http://127.0.0.1:1/; echo status=$?
